newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bond prices rise on U.S. jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Danish bond prices rise on U.S. jobs data.

text.p: Danish bond prices rose in early trade on Monday, in a delayed response to Friday's low U.S. jobless numbers which initially sent the market down.
Dealers expected the rise to continue if there were no new signals on the timetable for EMU from Monday's meeting of European Union finance and economy ministers in Luxembourg.
"We shall follow American prices up, if the EMU debate doesn't rise up again," a trader said.
He expected the rising prices to draw the Danish central bank into the market, offering paper in a range of maturities as it did on Friday.
At 0725 GMT the benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was up to 111.53, yielding 6.24 percent, from Friday's 111.27.
The seven percent 2007 bond, which becomes the benchmark on September 1, was up to 104.17, yielding 0.19 percent, compared to Friday's closing 103.96.
The 2006 yield gap to the 10-year German bund widened two basis points to 49 bp and the 2007-bund differential grew by the same amount to 67 bp.
The crown firmed to 3.8070 to the mark from Friday's 3.8076. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969650
